title: The North Star No.3 Express Leaving Ueno
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Yukiko Kudo, Yusaku Kudo, Inspector Nishimura) omitted by convention, consistent with the ep11 prototype's omission of Conan/Kogoro/Ran/Megure. This means one on-screen scene is NOT graphed as an edge: Kaetsu's attempted platform assault on Yukiko at Sapporo Station (she deliberately baited him to force a confession) has no valid non-omitted target node, so it is only referenced in Kaetsu's attrs rather than as a violent_action edge. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer for edges belonging to the same occurrence. The central mechanism (a body rigged with fishing line and released through a broken train window to fake a fleeing culprit's escape) mirrors a stolen, unfinished detective-novel manuscript (o9) that the culprit apparently read; the transcript never states outright whether Kaetsu was the unidentified third member of the original robbery trio that stole that manuscript, so that link is left as an open note rather than asserted as fact. case_type: murder.

objects.name: Yusaku Kudo's unpublished novel manuscript (stolen draft)

attrs.content: unfinished detective story in which an antique-store owner is murdered in a train tunnel using a body-drop trick to fake the culprit's escape
attrs.stolen: stolen roughly ten years earlier when a publishing-firm courier carrying the draft was robbed at a bank by Asama's gang
attrs.flaw_exploited: only the first half of the story was ever written; Kaetsu appears to have believed it was the complete, 'perfect' method and executed it without realizing the real plan had practical gaps (leftover luggage, tape residue) that gave him away

clues.desc: Timing contradiction: forensic reconstruction placed Asama's body falling from the train at ~4:10 AM, exactly matching witnesses' account of when the fleeing 'criminal' entered and left the room -- impossible for one person to simultaneously be a body already falling from the train and a figure fleeing on foot, which is what first proved the escape was mechanically staged rather than performed by a living person.

Comparative equipment clue: four different passengers each independently carried sporting/hobby gear (fishing tackle, a practice gun, kendo equipment, golf clubs) that could plausibly have supplied the tool for the vanishing-culprit trick -- only the fishing gear's owner actually matches the mechanism recovered from the body, narrowing four equally 'equipped' suspects down to one.
